analysis.title: USA: FOMC Leaves Fed Funds Rate Unchanged; Cook and Hammack Dissent Preferring a 25bp Hike
key_insights: The FOMC left the fed funds target range unchanged at 3.75-4.00% at its October meeting, following a 25bp hike at the September meeting.
Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, preferring a 25bp hike. Hammack also dissented in favor of a 25bp hike at the July meeting.

The statement reiterated that inflation 'remains elevated' and said 'the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal.'
The FOMC upgraded its description of economic activity to 'expanding at a strong pace', from 'solid' previously. The rest of the statement was unchanged from the September meeting.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Committee held rates after the September 25bp hike. Two dissents favored another 25bp hike, so the dissent signals a hawkish tilt within the Committee.

risk_factors: Inflation 'remains elevated', and two Committee members preferred a further 25bp hike, so further tightening is possible.
